transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 14:00 - 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (CedarBridge Channel Dir), Samir Khan (CedarBridge Head of Sales), Evelyn Brooks (CedarBridge Solutions Architect)

Summary: quick pipeline review, surface technical blockers, agree co-sell pricing anchors and owners, schedule technical deep-dive.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood here, schedule's tight so we'll run through the three priority deals then call out blockers. Nora, Samir, can you hear me?
[00:08] Nora Patel: Yep good to go, hear you fine.
[00:11] Samir Khan: All good. Morning for us, afternoon for you I think.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: Hi team, Liam from Redwood infra SE — I can jump in on tech stuff after the pipeline summary.
[00:22] Evelyn Brooks: Hey, Evelyn on the architecture side. Looking forward to the deep-dive later.

[02:00] Maya Chen: Quick agenda — 1) run through Deal A, B, C; 2) pricing / commission discussion; 3) tech fit, especially around private V-P-C and on-prem options; 4) next steps. Sound OK?
[02:12] Nora Patel: Yep sounds good. We'll start with Deal A — it's with Horizon Health, hospital chain, big POC budget but long procurement timelines.

[04:05] Samir Khan: For Horizon Health — it's a pilot for clinical summarization, about 500k ARR if it converts. Champion is Dr. Lee in clinical informatics. Main ask is data residency and SOC2 plus an on-prem option.
[04:40] Maya Chen: Got it. On the tech front, Liam — Redwood has Private with VPC and on-prem pack, we support KMS integration and audit logs. Any red flags if they want an air-gapped POC?
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: We can do on-prem, but we need to confirm kernel compatibility for the model they'll run. Also note sometimes our "Redwood Dedication" — I mean Dedicated — config needs larger GPU for batch inference; if it's a thousand concurrent chats it changes the sizing. For a clinical summarization POC it's usually OK but Evelyn we should verify the model size and token patterns.
[05:30] Evelyn Brooks: We're planning to run an LLM fine-tuned for summarization, roughly 13B parameters quantized to 4-bit. Sequence lengths are long — notes average 1,500 tokens. Concern is latency under 1.2s per call.
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: 1.2s is tight for 1.5k seq unless we do batching + prefix caching. We usually recommend sequence truncation or smart pre-tokenization. Also KV cache behavior on long contexts can blow memory; we might need to pin to a model variant or use a medium-sized instance with optimized attention kernels.

[08:00] Nora Patel: Procurement timeline is Q4 for Horizon but pilot by end of Q3. They want pricing anchors now. Samir any updates on pricing expectations?
[08:20] Samir Khan: They're expecting something in the market range; they mentioned a competitor (CompanyX) gave them a blended rate that looked lower but didn't include SLA or private deploy fees. We need a co-sell pricing that shows value but leaves room for partner margin.
[08:45] Maya Chen: We'll share a co-sell pricing spreadsheet — typical structure: list price for hosted + surcharge for private, partner commission band 15-25% depending on commitment. For on-prem, we often treat it as project-based + support. We'll send anchors after the call.

[10:10] Maya Chen: Deal B is with Atlas Retail — real-time product search and chat. This one is more latency-sensitive but smaller ARR, about 180k. They prefer a hosted Redwood API to start.
[10:30] Evelyn Brooks: Atlas uses 80k qps peaks during sales. They want autoscaling and burst guarantees. How does Redwood's Dedicated compare to BigCloudAI managed endpoints on autoscaling?
[10:55] Liam O'Connor: Our Dedicated pools are pre-warmed and we support burst capacity policies. There's a trade-off: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; hosted API is simpler but subject to shared capacity and throttles. For Atlas, Dedicated with a modest reserved commit and burst meta-policy should fit. We can also use model routing to cheaper variants at non-peak times.

[12:30] Samir Khan: Atlas is price-sensitive; if we demonstrate cost-saving via batching and model quant, they'll favor us. Can Redwood provide recommendations on quant profiles per workload?
[12:45] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize provides model and quantization recommendations by workload. We'll include recommended profiles for Atlas use-case in the doc Liam will share.

[14:10] Nora Patel: Deal C is an enterprise fintech — Cardinal Payments. This one's big if it goes, 1.2M ARR, but heavy security — PCI-adjacent, needs HSM/KMS integration and audit trails for every inference. They asked if we support separation of logs per tenant.
[14:40] Liam O'Connor: We do per-tenant audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations for key wrapping. For PCI adjacency we'll need to confirm encryption-in-transit + at-rest and role-based access controls. The tough part is they want a deterministic latency SLA for fraud scoring at 200ms which is challenging for larger models. We'll probably need a smaller specialized model for that path or a hybrid approach — rerank locally.

[16:00] Evelyn Brooks: They also asked about fallback behavior — if the dedicated pool is overloaded, can requests fall back to hosted or to a smaller model?
[16:15] Liam O'Connor: Yep, smart routing supports fallbacks by policy — region/cost/latency. We can set automatic fallback to a compatible variant. We'll capture policy examples in the follow-up doc.

[18:30] Maya Chen: Ok quick poll — which deals are highest priority to push this week? Samir?
[18:40] Samir Khan: Cardinal and Horizon are top, Atlas is second because of effort vs return. For Cardinal we need a security pack and a draft SOW.

[20:00] Nora Patel: On resourcing — CedarBridge expects to co-present in exec meetings. We should clarify who owns which artifacts and champions. Maya, can you share a co-sell narrative deck and one-pager?
[20:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll include a joint value prop slide, roles/responsibilities, and a suggested exec talking points doc.

[22:00] Samir Khan: A couple of objections we foresee: 1) price sensitivity vs market players; 2) skepticism about latency for long-context models; 3) procurement appetite for private on-prem projects. We should prep counterpoints.
[22:20] Maya Chen: For price, we show unit economics and total cost of ownership — Redwood Optimize recommendations often net 20-30% savings. For latency, we'll propose targeted perf benchmarks and a hybrid model approach. For procurement, we'll offer a phased SOW (pilot -> pilot expansion -> production) to reduce risk.

[25:00] Liam O'Connor: Technical ask — Evelyn, can you share a sample dataset or a representative transcript set for Horizon to run a quick benchmark? If you can't share PHI, anonymized samples are fine. That will let us pick kernel configs and give a realistic latency projection.
[25:20] Evelyn Brooks: Yes we can provide anonymized notes, probably ~2000 records. We'll aim to send that by next Tuesday.

[28:30] Maya Chen: Great. Pricing discussion — high level anchors: hosted API list X per token, private add-on Y per month, on-prem project starts at Z for initial setup. We'll post the detailed sheet. Partner commission: 20% standard for co-sell, higher for >1yr commit.
[30:00] Samir Khan: That commission band feels workable. We might need a margin carve for local discounts.

[33:10] Nora Patel: On enablement — any partner portal or sales enablement materials we can reuse?
[33:25] Maya Chen: We have partner enablement kit: slide decks, objection handling, ROI models. I'll drop links. Also a partner playbook for co-sell motions — steps for joint outreach, exec briefings, POC runbooks.

[36:00] Liam O'Connor: Quick note on benchmarks: if we're benchmarking 13B quantized with long contexts, we should expect throughput to vary widely across GPU families. If CedarBridge's customers require sub-second latencies at scale we might recommend a split architecture where short inference paths use a distilled 3-4B model and the summarization path uses the 13B model in async flow.

[39:10] Samir Khan: Good call. That hybrid approach could address Cardinal's 200ms SLA for fraud scoring while keeping summarization quality.

[42:00] Maya Chen: Let's lock owners — Maya will share pricing and partner collateral, Liam will run a perf bench and share notes, Samir will update pipeline and identify champions, Evelyn will send anonymized dataset for Horizon. We'll schedule the tech deep-dive week of 7/13 if that works.

[42:30] Nora Patel: Works for us. We prefer 7/15 for the deep-dive afternoon PST.

[45:00] Maya Chen: Noted — I'll propose a calendar invite for 2026-07-15 16:00 PST / 23:00 UTC and cc the appropriate folks.

[47:20] Samir Khan: One last thing — competitors. Horizon mentioned they were evaluating CompanyX and BigCloudAI. We should highlight Redwood's production controls and cost advantages. Also emphasize observability — token-level cost and latency breakdowns are big for procurement.

[47:50] Maya Chen: Agreed, observability is a strong differentiator. We'll include a screenshot of the console metrics in the co-sell deck (mock data).

[50:00] Evelyn Brooks: On security docs — can you share SOC2 and an architectural diagram for Private? Procurement will ask.
[50:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share SOC2 summary, architecture diagram and a compliance FAQ. I'll attach to the follow-up email.

[52:00] Nora Patel: Great, thanks everyone. Any other questions before we close?
[52:10] Samir Khan: None from me.
[52:15] Liam O'Connor: All good.
[52:20] Maya Chen: Okay recap of next steps and owners, we'll send notes and the pricing doc. Thanks all, talk soon.

[59:50] Call ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional ASR glitches ("Redwood Dedication" for Dedicated, "KV cash" for KV cache, VPC spoken as "V-P-C"). References to shared artifacts: co-sell pricing spreadsheet (link to be shared), partner playbook deck (link to be shared), anonymized dataset for benchmarks (to be uploaded to secure share by CedarBridge).
